A robot program just achieved this subgoal, verified by the camera:
  place object "red_block" (kind: block) on zone "orange_tray".
Program:
```python
obs = observe()
red_block = obs["objects"]["red_block"]
orange_tray = obs["zones"]["orange_tray"]
center = orange_tray["center"]
half_size = orange_tray["half_size"]

# Check if orange_tray is occupied
occupied = False
for name, obj in obs["objects"].items():
    if name == "red_block":
        continue
    if (abs(obj["center"][0] - center[0]) < half_size[0] and
        abs(obj["center"][1] - center[1]) < half_size[1] and
        obj["top_z"] > center[2] + 0.005):
        # Move the occupying object to purple_box
        place("purple_box", dx=0.02, dy=0.02)
        wait(20)
        occupied = True
        break

# Pick red_block
grasp_height = 0.02
yaw = red_block["long_axis_yaw"]
pick("red_block", grasp_height, yaw)
wait(20)

# Place on orange_tray
place("orange_tray")
wait(20)
```
Rewrite it as ONE reusable function

def place_on_zone_v3(obj_name, zone_name):

that calls observe() itself and computes every argument from the observation (no scene-specific
coordinates as literals; numeric offsets are fine). Keep what made it work.
Then, after the code, give a JSON object on the last line with the conditions under which you
expect the function to work, using only these keys:
{"object_kinds": [...], "requires_zone_free": true|false, "requires_gripper_empty": true|false,
  "notes": "<one sentence>"}
Format: a ```python block with the function, then the JSON line.

response:
```python
def place_on_zone_v3(obj_name, zone_name):
    obs = observe()
    obj = obs["objects"][obj_name]
    zone = obs["zones"][zone_name]
    center = zone["center"]
    half_size = zone["half_size"]

    # Check if the zone is occupied by any other object
    occupied = False
    for name, other_obj in obs["objects"].items():
        if name == obj_name:
            continue
        if (abs(other_obj["center"][0] - center[0]) < half_size[0] and
            abs(other_obj["center"][1] - center[1]) < half_size[1] and
            other_obj["top_z"] > center[2] + 0.005):
            # Move the occupying object to purple_box
            place("purple_box", dx=0.02, dy=0.02)
            wait(20)
            occupied = True
            break

    # Pick the target object
    grasp_height = 0.02
    yaw = obj["long_axis_yaw"]
    pick(obj_name, grasp_height, yaw)
    wait(20)

    # Place on the target zone
    place(zone_name)
    wait(20)
```
